title: Rumor claims the Oppo Reno17 series won't include a Pro model
description: The Oppo Reno17 series is rumored to launch in China next month. However, a new leak claims that the lineup will not include a Pro model, at least in India. Meanwhile, a hands-on image of the standard Reno17 has surfaced online. According to the leak, the Reno17 will retain most of its predecessor’s specifications and design. Oppo Reno17 leaked hands-on image The leak suggests that the Reno17 will feature the same Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 chipset and triple rear camera setup as the Reno16. title: Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China, but without Siri AI
description: Apple Intelligence was first announced in 2024 with iOS 18, but Apple struggled to make it available in two regions – the EU and China. Bloomberg reports that Cupertino will finally check the latter off the list with an upcoming update. iOS 27.3, which is expected in December, will enable Apple Intelligence for the Chinese market. While Apple uses Google’s Gemini in the West, it has struck a deal with Alibaba to use its Qwen and Tongyi Wanxiang models. Qwen is a general AI model and will likely power most features. However, Siri AI will reportedly not be part of the iOS 27.3...

title: HMD is going to withdraw from "select markets", rumor claims
description: According to a new rumor from a usually reliable source of information about HMD, the company is currently planning on withdrawing from "select markets". It will also allegedly "scale down production for its global device portfolio". HMD is said to be shifting its "core focus" to "regional markets" as well as the enterprise/industrial sector. The same source goes on to imply that there may be no further HMD global product launches this year. Presumably, that means the company will only be releasing devices on a market-by-market basis in the coming months. Of course, this is nothing...

title: OnePlus Ace 7 and Ace 7 Pro names confirmed by Google
description: The OnePlus Ace 7 had its specs leaked recently, and today, Google's official Supported Devices list has confirmed its name, while also revealing that it will have a sibling - the OnePlus Ace 7 Pro. According to Google's database, the Ace 7 has the model number PYF110, and the Ace 7 Pro has the model number PMS110. Both have run Geekbench 7 multiple times over the past few days, with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset at the helm. title: Leaked OnePlus Ace 7 schematic shows its dual-airflow cooling setup
description: A recent leak suggested that the upcoming OnePlus Ace 7 would feature a built-in active cooling fan. Now, a tipster has shared alleged schematics of the phone, offering a look at its new cooling system. Tipster Digital Chat Station shared the details in a Weibo post, claiming that the OnePlus Ace 7 will debut a new dual-airflow cooling system. According to the tipster, the dual-airflow system will direct hot air out through the sides while pushing cool air towards the rear panel. title: Leak: images and specs of Samsung's upcoming Android XR smart glasses surface
description: Samsung first announced its AI smart glasses back in July and we even got some hands-on time with them. However, they are still nowhere to be seen – the latest rumor (not even official info) is that they will launch in November. Now, thanks to SammyGuru, we can have a look at the different designs that Samsung’s partners from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have created. Even better, there are finally some details about the hardware – the initial announcement only mentioned that the glasses run Android XR on a Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 chipset. description: Samsung has released the Android 17-based One UI 9 stable update for the Galaxy S23, Galaxy S23+, Galaxy S23 Ultra, Galaxy Z Fold5, and Galaxy Z Flip5. title: Apple's website hints the full-size HomePod could get Siri AI
description: Yesterday was a busy day for Apple's smart home efforts. The company unveiled the HomeView smart display, the new Apple TV 4K, the HomePod mini 2, and the Apple Home Collection. All three of Apple's new devices support Siri AI, but what about the older full-size HomePod? Thankfully, Apple's own website suggests it may not be left out after all. A tipster on X noticed that the product page for the second-generation HomePod was updated yesterday. title: AT&T is selling its Mexican business for $2 billion
description: AT&T has been one of Mexico's biggest carriers for over a decade, but that's about to come to an end. The company has announced that it has reached an agreement to sell AT&T Mexico to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2 billion in cash at closing, "subject to certain adjustments", plus "additional contractual and contingent benefits". The buyer is a consortium owned 50/50 by Televisa and Fintech, which plans to pay with a combination of cash on hand and debt financing. What it's getting is Mexico's second-largest mobile operator, with about 24.7 million wireless subscribers at the...

description: Google is starting to sell hardware on its Play Store. In some regions, the company has quietly added a new "Shop devices" tab in the Play Store's account switcher. The interesting bit is that Google is listing not only Pixel devices, but Samsung's too. Users can buy the Galaxy S26 lineup and some Galaxy Watch8 devices in addition to Pixel 11 series phones and Pixel Watches. title: Samsung Galaxy A58's camera details surface, and they are nothing to get excited about
description: Samsung unveiled the Galaxy A57 in March, and it is already working on the Galaxy A58, which could arrive in March or April next year. There is no word from Samsung about the Galaxy A58, but a new report from GalaxyClub shares its camera details, and they are nothing to get excited about. According to the Dutch publication, the Samsung Galaxy A58 will feature a 50MP primary camera, a 12MP ultrawide camera, a 5MP macro camera, and a 12MP selfie camera. title: Nothing is reportedly working on smart glasses - ones with a camera and ones without
description: Nothing, the smartphone company that has only launched three mid-rangers this year ((4a), (4a) Pro and (4b)), has been distracting itself with other gadgets. Earlier this week, it unveiled new Bluetooth speakers. And now Roland Quandt says that Carl Pei & co. are working on not one but two kinds of smart glasses. One will be the more capable camera-equipped type of smart glasses. They will have ChatGPT, translation and other features. title: Google Play for cars brings Firefox, background playback for YouTube and more
description: Google has cooked up a new update to improve the Android Automotive experience – the update brings a redesigned interface and support for new apps including the Firefox browser, plus multiple entertainment apps. With this update, you will be able to browse the web using Firefox (Chrome and Vivaldi are also available). You will also be able to stream shows on the Starz and JioHotstar apps or play Ludo King. description: Oppo launched the Find X10 Pro Max and Find X10 in China on September 22, and they are set to launch globally later this month. Today, the company has started teasing that global debut with a short video focused on what it calls "true-to-life imaging". It posits that over the years smartphone imaging has kept getting brighter, sharper, and more vibrant, and we're now at a point where "sometimes our photos don't look the way we remember" them. description: The Honor Win2 series, comprising the Win2, Win RT2, and Win Turbo 2, is set to launch in China next week. After revealing the designs and color options of all three phones yesterday, Honor has now confirmed some of their key specifications. Honor has confirmed that the Win2 will be powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset. The phone will pack a 10,100mAh battery and feature a 2K resolution display with a 185Hz refresh rate and 5,920Hz PWM dimming. The updates will initially focus on features that help users translate, summarize, and transcribe content. In a press release, Samsung confirmed that Galaxy AI features such as Call Assist, Interpreter, Note Assist, and Transcript Assist will add support for Malay and Hungarian.
